articles.title: Rupee gains 96 paise, but Nifty falls 157 points on crude, FII outflows
articles.excerpt:
Indian equities closed lower on Monday as elevated crude oil prices, persistent foreign fund outflows and rising bond yields weighed on sentiment, offsetting the rupee’s sharp appreciation against the US dollar.

The Nifty 50 fell 157.10 points, or 0.70 per cent, to close at 22,363.35, while the Sensex declined 547.65 points, or 0.76 per cent, to 71,924.68. The Bank Nifty shed 338.65 points, or 0.61 per cent, to settle at 54,918.

The Nifty opened 70 points higher and touched an intraday high of 22,651.10 before reversing course as selling pressure emerged.

articles.title: SEBI’s Credit Risk-o-Meter may make bond risks easier to compare
articles.excerpt:
The Securities and Exchange Board of India’s (SEBI) new Credit Risk-o-Meter could make it easier for retail investors to compare debt investments by translating credit ratings into six colour-coded risk categories, addressing a common difficulty in interpreting ratings assigned by different credit rating agencies.

The regulator has mandated, effective in 45 days, the meter for listed and proposed-to-be-listed non-convertible securities, commercial papers, securitised debt instruments, security receipts and structured debt or market-linked debentures, whether issued through public issues or private placements.

articles.title: India benchmark bond posts worst day in six months on RBI measures
articles.excerpt:
Indian government bonds experienced a significant decline due to central bank measures aimed at draining liquidity. The benchmark 10-year bond yield rose to its highest level in three years, signaling potential rate hikes. Consumer inflation increased to 5.54%, exceeding forecasts and raising concerns over future monetary policy. The Reserve Bank of India announced bond sales and changes to cash reserve ratio maintenance.
